questions.q:
With reference to the Sankosh river, recently in news after a glacial lake outburst flood in Bhutan, consider the following statements:
1. It is known as the Puna Tsang Chu in Bhutan.
2. It joins the Brahmaputra near Gauripur.
3. It is formed by the confluence of the Pho Chu and the Mo Chu.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: All three are correct. In India the river forms part of the Assam-West Bengal boundary. In October 2026 a GLOF upstream in Bhutan put the Sankosh on red alert and more than 10,000 people were moved to safety in West Bengal's Alipurduar district, adding to concern over GLOF preparedness after the 2023 Sikkim disaster.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Yenisei river:
1. It flows from south to north across central Siberia into the Kara Sea.
2. Its tributary, the Angara, drains Lake Baikal.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Both are correct. The Yenisei forms from the Great and Little Yenisei at Kyzyl and is the largest river system draining to the Arctic. It was in news for brown-bear attacks near Podtesovo. Like the Ob and the Lena (static GK), it flows north, so spring ice-melt upstream causes floods against still-frozen lower reaches.

questions.q:
With reference to Ghana, whose Cabinet approved seeking BRICS membership, consider the following statements:
1. The Equator passes through Ghana.
2. Lake Volta, among the largest artificial lakes, was formed by the Kariba Dam.
3. Ghana shares a land border with Nigeria.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: None is correct. The Prime Meridian, not the Equator, passes through Ghana, and Lake Volta was formed by the Akosombo Dam (Kariba is on the Zambezi, static GK). Ghana borders Cote d'Ivoire, Burkina Faso and Togo; Togo and Benin separate it from Nigeria. It lies on the Gulf of Guinea and exports gold, cocoa and oil.

questions.q: Zuqar Island, near which Houthis said Saudi forces targeted a yacht with 14 Indians nearby, lies close to which one of the following straits?
questions.e: Zuqar, in the Hanish archipelago of the Red Sea, lies near Bab-el-Mandeb. Eritrea seized it in 1995, and an arbitral tribunal awarded it to Yemen in 1998. It is a shield volcano with pahoehoe lava. Bab-el-Mandeb links the Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden, a route vital for India's trade with Europe.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Macquarie Island:
1. It is the only place where rocks from the Earth's mantle are being actively exposed above sea level.
2. It lies in the Arctic Ocean north of Norway.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 1 is correct. Macquarie is a sub-Antarctic island about 1,500 km south-east of Tasmania, on the Macquarie Ridge at the Pacific-Indo-Australian plate boundary, and a UNESCO site since 1997. It was in news for Australia's first H5N1 case, found in elephant seals.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Place in news : Location
1. Zavodovski Island : South Sandwich Islands
2. Lake Untersee : Antarctica
3. Bonin (Ogasawara) Islands : About 1,000 km south of Tokyo
4. Sakurajima : Kagoshima Bay, Kyushu
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: All four pairs are correct. Chinstrap penguins on Zavodovski fell about 63% in 14 years. Lake Untersee, fed by the Anuchin Glacier, rose about 2 m after a 2019 flood. The Bonins had an M 6.5 quake, and Sakurajima, an andesitic stratovolcano joined to the Osumi Peninsula by its 1914 eruption, sent up a thick ash plume.

questions.q:
With reference to places in news in India, consider the following statements:
1. Ujani Dam, where a community project is removing invasive fish, is on the Bhima river in Solapur district.
2. Kariyachalli Island, protected by artificial reef modules, is part of the Gulf of Mannar Marine National Park.
3. Trishna Wildlife Sanctuary, where Phayre's leaf monkey was recorded, is in Mizoram.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; Trishna (est. 1988) is in South Tripura. Kariyachalli, one of 21 islands of the Gulf of Mannar park, shrank from 20.85 ha in 1969 to about 3.14 ha in 2025, and 8,500 IIT-Madras reef modules under the TN SHORE project aim to halt erosion. Ujani (1980) lies on a Krishna tributary.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Pong Dam, in news over fishing boats in a restricted zone:
1. It is a gravity dam on the Sutlej river in Bilaspur district.
2. Its reservoir is known as Gobind Sagar.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Neither is correct. Pong is an earth-fill dam on the Beas in Kangra, built in 1961-74; its reservoir, Maharana Pratap Sagar, became a bird sanctuary in 1983 and a Ramsar site in 2002. Gobind Sagar is the reservoir of the Bhakra dam on the Sutlej in Bilaspur (static GK).

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Oil field : Country/region
1. Ghawar : Saudi Arabia
2. Tengiz : Western Siberia, Russia
3. Daqing : Heilongjiang, China
4. Prudhoe Bay : Gulf of Mexico
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1 and 3 are correct. Tengiz is in Kazakhstan, on the north-east Caspian near Atyrau, and exports via the Caspian Pipeline Consortium; Russia's largest field is Samotlor in Western Siberia. Prudhoe Bay is on Alaska's North Slope, while Cantarell lies in the Bay of Campeche. Ghawar is the world's largest conventional field.

questions.q: Which oil field is described as the second-largest offshore field in the world, developed on four artificial islands?
questions.e: Upper Zakum lies offshore in the Persian Gulf north-west of Abu Dhabi, found in 1963 and operated by ADNOC. Burgan in Kuwait is the world's largest sandstone reservoir and second-largest field after Ghawar; Rumaila is Iraq's largest; Cantarell, in the Bay of Campeche, owes its reservoir rock to the Chicxulub impact.

questions.q:
With reference to the proposed concept of 'heat storms', consider the following statements:
1. 'Heat storm' is an official category of the World Meteorological Organization.
2. The largest such event, 'Vera', lasted 367 days in 2023-24 and covered nearly 85% of the globe.
3. The frequency of such events rose from about five a year in the 1960s to about 102 a year this decade.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. The term was proposed after a Reuters analysis of hourly global temperatures since 1960 and consultation with researchers; it is not an IMD or WMO category. A heat storm is a large, long, multi-regional heat event; a 'heat cascade' is a series of them. Causes include persistent high pressure, El Nino and dry-soil feedback.

questions.q:
With reference to Cyclone Arnab, consider the following statements:
1. It was the first North Indian Ocean cyclone of 2026.
2. Its name was proposed by Bangladesh.
3. It crossed the Andhra Pradesh coast between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam on 28 October 2026.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: All three are correct. Arnab, Bengali for 'sea', intensified rapidly into a very severe cyclonic storm with winds of 125-135 km/h and stayed nearly stationary near Narsapur and Yanam for about six hours after landfall; Visakhapatnam got 217 mm. Names come from a 13-country list adopted in 2020 and are assigned by IMD as RSMC New Delhi.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: In El Nino years, Bay of Bengal cyclones tend to track towards Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu rather than Odisha and West Bengal.
Statement-II: The name 'Arnab' was proposed by Bangladesh.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I. The shift in tracks comes from cyclones forming closer to the equator in El Nino years; warmer seas also allow rapid intensification, as with Arnab when Nino 3.4 was 2-2.8 degrees above normal. Hudhud (2014) also hit Andhra Pradesh in an El Nino year.

questions.q: Jawahar Dweep (Butcher Island), recently declared India's first single-use-plastic-free marine oil terminal, is located in
questions.e: Jawahar Dweep lies in Mumbai harbour near the Gateway of India and is a key crude and product terminal of Mumbai Port. Ports handle large volumes of plastic packaging and waste, so the declaration is part of wider efforts to cut marine plastic pollution.
